Issued at 134 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

Pattern / Forecast Synopsis: 

Occluding cyclone over the Dakotas into the Canadian Prairies will 
continue to move north and east atop a 500mb ridge axis peaking 
right overhead through today. Result will be a pinching of the 
pressure gradient today, and an upward trend in warm advection via 
breezy SW flow. A weak cold front will stall just to our north and 
west tonight, with the baroclinic zone inching ever so closer. As 
such, anticipating a series of quick moving low pressure systems to 
pass through the Great Lakes riding the front and forcing it 
eastward... the first passes well to our north and west early 
Saturday, leading to the reinvigoration of breezy SW flow and a 
renewed warm advection regime. The second will pass essentially 
overhead Sunday, which will lead to the next chances for rain across 
the area as the cold front passes through. Colder air begins to 
build into the region through later Sunday afternoon in the wake of 
the initial cold frontal passage. A secondary cold front surges 
through the area Sunday night, bringing with it a much colder 
airmass and an outside shot at some snowflakes. Stout area of high 
pressure over the Canadian Prairies lurches south and east into the 
Great Lakes, quickly bringing a return of drier air to the region, 
but given the Canadian origin of the airmass, seasonably cold 
airmass will be established for the holiday week.

Details: 

Wind / Temperature Trends: Anticipation is that breezy to even windy 
conditions build as warm advection shifts into overdrive for today. 
Result will be temperatures spiking to upper 50s / near 60 for our 
friends north of the Big Bridge, and temperatures near / just above 
60 across northern lower (outside shot at some mid 60s in 
downsloping locales). Aside from the warmth, the big story will be 
the aforementioned winds... which at times could easily gust over 
30mph across eastern upper. Along and west of I-75 in northern 
lower, could see a few rogue gusts in excess of 35mph. For our 
friends in the rest of northern lower, probably more like 20 to 25 
mph gusts. Winds slacken tonight as the initial system zips toward 
James Bay and northern Quebec and the pressure gradient eases for 
Friday. A few degrees cooler Friday but with continued drier 
conditions. Next series of systems builds Saturday, with the warmest 
surge of air building ahead. Winds once again trend upward, with 
another period of 25 to 35mph gusts (again strongest N/W), 
accompanied by temperatures spiking well into the 60s... with a few 
record highs in reach (namely at GLR and PLN, where weather records 
are shortest in archive). 

As the next systems pass through, winds generally turn NW through 
the day Sunday (still a bit breezy), but will bring sharply cooler 
air into the region. With a somewhat slower trend in things, 
anticipation is that a pretty healthy gradient in temps sets up with 
highs in the upper 40s to lower 50s in eastern upper and far NW 
lower, while areas in northeast lower make another run at 60. Timing 
of the front will dictate if/when a temperature crash happens Sunday 
afternoon. Nonetheless, by the time Monday rolls around, we will be 
in a much more seasonable temperature regime, with highs in the 30s 
to lower 40s and overnight lows in the low-to-mid 20s... a trend 
that looks to ever so slowly moderate as we head toward Thanksgiving 
itself.

Rain / Precip Chances: Dry weather prevails through Saturday before 
the next system drums up a quality surge of moisture and lift across 
the region. Rain showers set to prevail from late Saturday night 
through the day Sunday as the surface low essentially passes right 
through the region. Transient nature of any convectively influenced 
showers should lead to minimal rainfall, with most areas struggling 
to attain much more than 0.25". Secondary cold frontal passage 
Sunday night into early Monday morning may bring just enough colder 
air into the region to overlap with synoptic moisture to force some 
snow showers into northwest lower and eastern upper... but owing to 
the limited moisture as it is... not anticipating this to be all 
that impactful for the Monday morning commute. Increasingly drier 
airmass will complicate the development of any lake effect snow 
showers Monday, with drier conditions likely to prevail through at 
least Thanksgiving... weaker moisture starved wave may try to make a 
run at the region, but will likely struggle to produce much outside 
of some additional cloud cover (barring changes in trends).
